guide.title: Westminster, London: the Abbey, Parliament, Trafalgar Square, Buckingham Palace and Regent's Park
guide.intro: The City of Westminster is a London borough, and it holds the state quarter of the country. Westminster Abbey and the Palace of Westminster face each other across Parliament Square inside a World Heritage Site inscribed in 1987, NHLE 1000095, and Whitehall runs north from them past the Banqueting House to Trafalgar Square, where two national collections and a parish church marking its 300th anniversary in 2026 stand on one square. The Strand carries the borough east to Somerset House and the City boundary. St James's and Mayfair hold Buckingham Palace, Burlington House and Apsley House, and north of Oxford Street the crowds thin at Hertford House and at Nash's park with its terraces, boating lake and zoo. The National Heritage List for England records 4,003 listed-building entries inside the City of Westminster boundary as mapped by OpenStreetMap relation 51781, 206 of them at Grade I.

sections.heading: Westminster, Whitehall and Millbank
sections.body:
The state quarter. Westminster Abbey and the Palace of Westminster stand across Parliament Square from one another, Whitehall runs north past the Banqueting House and the Cenotaph to the war rooms under the Treasury, and the river walk leads south to Tate Britain at Millbank, with Victoria and the Byzantine cathedral inland to the west.

Westminster Abbey, at 20 Dean's Yard, SW1P 3PA, is listed Grade I as NHLE 1291494 under the name Westminster Abbey (The Collegiate Church of St Peter). General Admittance runs 9.30am to 3.30pm Monday to Friday and 9am to 1pm on Saturday, and the abbey publishes no General Admittance slot at all on Sunday, when St Margaret's Church opens 11am to 2pm, the Cellarium 9am to 3pm, the Kiosk 10am to 5pm and the Shop 9.30am to 4.30pm. Admission in the operator's 17 June to 24 June and 2 September to 30 September 2026 band is £31 for an adult, £28 for a visitor aged 65 and over and £28 for a student, £14 for a child aged 6 to 17 and free under 5, and it covers the cloisters, College Garden, Chapter House and Pyx Chamber. The abbey has been the coronation church since 1066 and is the resting place of 17 monarchs; the church standing today was begun by Henry III in 1245, the West Towers were completed in 1745 in Portland stone to a design by Nicholas Hawksmoor, and the most recent major restoration ran from 1973 to 1995. Three designations of three different types cover this fabric: the Grade I listing, NHLE 1291494; the World Heritage Site 'Palace of Westminster, Westminster Abbey and St Margaret's Church', NHLE 1000095, which carries no grade; and the scheduled monument covering the Chapter House and Pyx Chamber in the cloisters, NHLE 1003579, which carries no grade either. The Great Cloisters, including St Faith's Chapel, the Chapter House, the Parlour and the Dormitory, are covered by a further Grade I listing, NHLE 1066370.

The Palace of Westminster, SW1A 0AA, is Grade I as NHLE 1226284 under the name Houses of Parliament and The Palace of Westminster, and is the first element named in the same World Heritage Site. It was rebuilt from 1840 by Charles Barry, with interiors by A.W.N. Pugin, after the old palace burned in 1834. Audio tour tickets start at £31 for an adult with one child free, and Parliament states that its Inside the UK Parliament guided tours are free for UK residents. The Church of St Margaret, Westminster, the third element of the World Heritage Site, is Grade I, NHLE 1226286. The medieval Jewel Tower across Abingdon Street carries two designations of different types and they must not be merged: a Grade I listing, NHLE 1225529, named THE JEWEL HOUSE (OR TOWER) OF THE PALACE OF WESTMINSTER, and a scheduled monument, NHLE 1003580, which carries no grade. The Cenotaph in Whitehall is Grade I, NHLE 1357354, and eight telephone kiosks, two K2 and six K6, stand outside the former HM Treasury building under one Grade II entry, NHLE 1393340.

Banqueting House, Whitehall, SW1A 2ER, is Grade I as NHLE 1357353 and is described by Historic Royal Palaces as the survivor of the lost Palace of Whitehall. Its opening is limited: a summer opening from 1 August to 20 September 2026, plus separate Open Days and Members-Only Days, with an adult ticket at £10.00 and children aged 5 to 15 free. The operator's own headline subjects are the Rubens ceiling, Inigo Jones's architecture, the Undercroft and the site of Charles I's execution. Horse Guards stands about 95 m north-west across Whitehall and is separately Grade I, NHLE 1066100; the Grade I Treasury Buildings, holding the Cabinet Office and the Privy Council Office, are NHLE 1267063. Churchill War Rooms occupies the basement of a different Whitehall block, the New Government Offices (HM Treasury) at Clive Steps, King Charles Street, SW1A 2AQ: the Grade II* listing is of that host building, NHLE 1066103, under the name New Government Offices (HM Treasury) and archway link with Foreign Office at east end of King Charles Street. Imperial War Museums opens it 9.30am to 6pm with last entry at 5pm, every day except 24 to 26 December, at £34 for an adult with members and under-fives free, and describes the rooms as left as they were in 1945, under 12 feet of concrete and steel. The Grade II statue of Sir Winston Churchill stands about 250 m away in Parliament Square, NHLE 1392374.

Tate Britain, at Millbank, SW1P 4RG, is Grade II* as NHLE 1222913 under the entry name TATE GALLERY, and opens Monday to Sunday 10.00 to 18.00 with entry free and no need to book. It was built on the site of the former Millbank prison after a decision in 1892, to a design by Sidney Smith and with an anonymous donation from Henry Tate; the National Gallery of British Art, as it was then called, was opened by the Prince of Wales on 21 July 1897 and opened to the public on 16 August 1897. Westminster Cathedral, at 42 Francis Street, SW1P 1QW, is Grade I as NHLE 1066500 and opens daily 7.30am to 7pm, with Mass on Sunday at 8am, 10am sung, 12 noon solemn, 5.30pm and 7pm. It is the Roman Catholic Metropolitan Cathedral of the Most Precious Blood and the seat of the Archbishop of Westminster, and it states that it receives no funding from the Vatican.

sections.heading: Trafalgar Square, the Strand and Covent Garden
sections.body:
The free-museum belt. Two national collections and a working parish church stand on one square; the Strand runs east past Somerset House to the City boundary, and Covent Garden's piazza and opera house sit a few streets north.

Trafalgar Square, WC2N 5DU, is a Grade I registered park and garden, NHLE 1001362, and the Nelson Monument, or Nelson's Column, is a separate Grade I listing, NHLE 1276052. Registered parks and gardens carry a grade, so the square is written as a registered landscape rather than as a listed building. The Grade I statue of James II stands in front of the National Gallery's west wing, NHLE 1217629. Charing Cross Underground station is 49 m from the centre of the square.

The National Gallery, at Trafalgar Square, WC2N 5DN, with its visitor entrance in the Sainsbury Wing, is Grade I as NHLE 1066236; the Sainsbury Wing is a separate Grade I entry of its own, NHLE 1451082. It opens daily 10am to 6pm and until 9pm on Friday, closing 24 to 26 December and 1 January, and general admission is free. The gallery holds the national collection of paintings in the Western European tradition from the 13th to the 19th centuries, over 2,600 works, and states that its paintings are on show 361 days a year free of charge. It has undergone many transformations since its foundation in 1824, and a new Research Centre is opening in 2028. The National Portrait Gallery, on St Martin's Place, WC2H 0HE, is a separate Grade I entry, NHLE 1066285, standing immediately north-east of the National Gallery. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here. St Martin-in-the-Fields, on Trafalgar Square, WC2N 4JJ, is Grade I as NHLE 1217661 under the name CHURCH OF ST MARTIN IN THE FIELDS; the church is marking its 300th anniversary in 2026 and publishes its hours only two weeks ahead, so they change week to week. In the week commencing 7 September it opened 8.30am to 5pm on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 8.30am to 7.30pm on Wednesday, 10.30am to 5pm on Saturday and 9am to 6pm on Sunday, with the Cafe in the Crypt keeping its own separate hours. Read the entry names on this square: the churchyard walls and railings are a separate Grade I entry, NHLE 1066237, a churchyard wall adjoining the crypt entrance is Grade II, NHLE 1264028, the John Law Baker memorial drinking fountain is Grade II, NHLE 1248613, and a drinking fountain attached to the church walls is Grade II, NHLE 1277825. The Grade II* St Martin's Vestry Hall, NHLE 1264790, St Martin's Vicarage, NHLE 1264791, and St Martin in the Fields Secondary School, NHLE 1236019, stand in the same block.

Somerset House, on the Strand, WC2R 1LA, is Grade I as NHLE 1237041 under the name SOMERSET HOUSE AND KING'S COLLEGE OLD BUILDING, an entry that covers the university building at the east end as well as the courtyard blocks. It is open to everyone seven days a week, 8am to 11pm, and its courtyard is the Edmond J. Safra Fountain Court. The City of London boundary runs east along the Strand from here, and the Grade I Church of St Mary le Strand, NHLE 1236753, stands in the roadway between; the Grade II* Savoy Chapel, the Queen's Chapel of the Savoy, is NHLE 1264731 and the Grade II Savoy Hotel is NHLE 1236709, both on the same stretch. The Royal Opera House, on Bow Street, WC2E 9DD, is Grade I as NHLE 1066392 and is home to The Royal Ballet, The Royal Opera and The Orchestra of the Royal Opera House. It opens daily from 12 noon and closes after the evening performance; with no evening performance it closes at 11pm Monday to Saturday and 9pm on Sunday. Auditoriums open 30 minutes before each performance and the box office opens Monday to Saturday from 12 noon until the start of the evening performance or 6pm. The operator states that over one million people come through its doors each year and that it runs over 1,250 schools, community programmes and affordable performances. The Grade II* Covent Garden Market Building, NHLE 1066949, is about 100 m from the opera house, and the Grade I Church of St Paul, Covent Garden, is NHLE 1066487.

sections.heading: St James's, Mayfair and the Royal Parks
sections.body:
Court and club London. Buckingham Palace stands at the end of the Mall with St James's Park in front of it, and Piccadilly runs west past Burlington House to Hyde Park Corner and Wellington's house, with the Royal Albert Hall and the Albert Memorial on the Kensington Gore frontage of the parks.

Buckingham Palace, SW1A 1AA, is Grade I as NHLE 1239087, and its grounds are separately a Grade II* registered park and garden, NHLE 1000795. The State Rooms open to visitors each summer and the 2026 dates are 9 July to 27 September: opening at 9:30 with last admission 17:30 and closing 19:30 to 31 August, then last admission 16:30 and closing 18:30 from 1 to 27 September, with the palace closed on Tuesdays and Wednesdays through September. From October to May it opens only on selected dates for small guided tours, starting at various times between 10:00 and 15:30 and lasting around 1 hour 30 minutes. Standard admission is £33.00, or £37.00 with a donation. The Royal Collection Trust states that Queen Victoria was the first sovereign to live in the palace, in 1837, and that the White Drawing Room will not be accessible during the 2026 Summer Opening because of the Buckingham Palace Reservicing programme. The curtilage here is extreme and the entry names matter: at least a dozen further entries on the National Heritage List for England carry Buckingham Palace in their name, among them the Grade I Royal Mews, NHLE 1066364, the Grade I Riding School, NHLE 1239207, the Grade I Summer House in the garden, NHLE 1239210, the Grade I Waterloo Vase, NHLE 1239244, and four Grade II lamp posts at the gateway to the Royal Mews, NHLE 1239206. The Queen Victoria Memorial facing the palace is Grade I, NHLE 1273864, and its gates, gatepiers, balustrades and fountain are a further Grade I entry, NHLE 1239086.

St James's Park, on The Mall, SW1Y 5AA, is a Grade I registered park and garden, NHLE 1000483, with pedestrian gates open 5am to midnight. It is one of five Grade I registered parks and gardens in the borough, with The Regent's Park, NHLE 1000246, Kensington Gardens, NHLE 1000340, Hyde Park, NHLE 1000814, and Trafalgar Square, NHLE 1001362; Green Park is Grade II*, NHLE 1000806. The Royal Parks, which manages it, describes its estate as covering over 5,000 acres of historic parkland. The park links Buckingham Palace at its west end to Horse Guards Parade at its east, with the Whitehall block between.

The Royal Academy of Arts, at Burlington House, Piccadilly, W1J 0BD, is Grade II* as NHLE 1226676 under the name Royal Academy including Burlington House and Galleries and Royal Academy Schools Buildings; a second Grade II* entry, NHLE 1291018, is named simply Royal Academy of Arts. It closes on Monday and opens Tuesday to Saturday 10am to 6pm and until 9pm on Friday, and the operator publishes no Sunday row at all. Visitors are asked to use the Burlington House entrance until Spring 2027 while 6 Burlington Gardens is closed. The RA was founded in 1768 by a group of 40 artists and architects who became the first Royal Academicians, with Sir Joshua Reynolds as its first president, and it keeps free displays including the John Madejski Fine Rooms and the Collection Gallery. The Grade II Burlington Arcade next door is NHLE 1066338 and the Grade II* Ritz Hotel is NHLE 1226499.

Apsley House, at 149 Piccadilly, Hyde Park Corner, W1J 7NT, is Grade I as NHLE 1226873 and English Heritage opens it Wednesday to Sunday 11am to 5pm, with last entry at 4.30pm. Robert Adam designed and built it between 1771 and 1778 for Lord Chancellor Henry, 1st Baron Apsley, later 2nd Earl Bathurst, at a cost of £10,000; Wellington bought the freehold in January 1830 for £9,532, and Benjamin Dean Wyatt's final bill for the new staircase and the Waterloo Gallery on the west front exceeded £64,000. The Wellington Museum Act was signed in 1947 and the house opened to the public in 1952, the centenary of the death of the 1st Duke of Wellington. Its collection includes work by Velazquez, Rubens, Goya, Titian and Bruegel. The Royal Albert Hall stands on Kensington Gore, in the City of Westminster, and is Grade I as NHLE 1217742; the three lamp standards outside it are Grade II entries in their own right and are not part of that entry. The Albert Memorial, Grade I, NHLE 1217741, stands on the same frontage and is also in the City of Westminster; Kensington Palace, 900 m west, is in Kensington and Chelsea, and the borough boundary runs between the palace and the gardens.

sections.heading: Marylebone and Regent's Park
sections.body:
North of Oxford Street the crowds thin. A private collection kept in the house it was assembled in, and Nash's park with its stucco terraces, boating lake and zoo.

The Wallace Collection is at Hertford House, Manchester Square, W1U 3BN, and opens daily 10.00 to 17.00, closing on 24, 25 and 26 December, with entry to the permanent collection free. It is a national museum of painting, sculpture, furniture, arms and armour, and porcelain, built over the 18th and 19th centuries by the Marquesses of Hertford and Sir Richard Wallace and given to the British nation in 1897 by Lady Wallace so that it could be kept together. The grades here run the wrong way round from what a visitor expects: Hertford House is Grade II, NHLE 1239252, its forecourt walls, gate piers and railings are a separate Grade II entry, NHLE 1239308, and the drinking fountain in the forecourt is Grade II*, NHLE 1277828. Manchester Square itself, with Portman Square, is a Grade II registered park and garden, NHLE 1000820.

The Regent's Park is entered from the Inner Circle, NW1 4NR, and is a Grade I registered park and garden, NHLE 1000246. Its pedestrian gates open 5am to 8pm and its vehicle gates 7am to midnight. The Royal Parks records over 120 species of bird in the park each year, 5,000 varieties of tree, areas of wild meadow, historic grasslands and a breeding population of hedgehogs. The park lies in the City of Westminster; Primrose Hill, which The Royal Parks manages together with it as one operational unit, lies north of the Regent's Canal in Camden and is Camden's. The Nash terraces around the Outer Circle are listed at Grade I in their own right: 1-43 Clarence Terrace is NHLE 1357311.

ZSL London Zoo stands inside the park, off the Outer Circle. Its main entrance, the boating lake and the Inner Circle side are in the City of Westminster, and the northern fringe along the Outer Circle is in Camden. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here. Four structures at the zoo are on the National Heritage List for England: the Elephant and Rhinoceros Pavilion, Grade II*, NHLE 1323694; the Snowdon Aviary, Grade II*, NHLE 1323695; the west footbridge, Grade II, NHLE 1119765; and the London Zoo War Memorial, Grade II, NHLE 1434655.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
Twenty-nine distinct stations stand inside the City of Westminster, and there is no single interchange for the borough. A count of named railway=station features on OpenStreetMap gives 33, but Paddington appears three times under three names and Marylebone and Victoria twice each; the unit that matters to a traveller is the station, and there are 29. Four National Rail termini are inside the borough: Charing Cross, served by Southeastern; Marylebone, served by Chiltern Railways; Paddington, served by Great Western Railway and Heathrow Express; and Victoria, served by Gatwick Express, Southeastern, Southern and Thameslink. Three Elizabeth line stations serve it — Paddington, Bond Street and Tottenham Court Road, the last straddling the Camden boundary. Westminster has no Overground station, no DLR station and no tram stop: Queen's Park, which carries both the Bakerloo line and the Overground Lioness line, is in Brent, and so are Kensal Green and Kilburn Park.

For Westminster, Whitehall and Millbank, take the Circle, District or Jubilee line to Westminster, 265 m from the Houses of Parliament, 297 m from Churchill War Rooms and 298 m from both Westminster Abbey and the Banqueting House. St James's Park, on the Circle and District lines, is 420 m from the war rooms and 462 m from the abbey. Embankment is 377 m from the Banqueting House and Charing Cross 411 m. For Tate Britain, Pimlico on the Victoria line is 479 m, and Vauxhall, across the river in Lambeth, is 511 m and the nearest National Rail station to the gallery, served by South Western Railway. For Westminster Cathedral, Victoria Underground is 219 m and London Victoria rail station 327 m, with St James's Park 593 m. Waterloo, in Lambeth across Westminster Bridge, carries the Bakerloo, Jubilee, Northern and Waterloo & City lines beneath South Western Railway's terminus and is 893 m from the Houses of Parliament.

For Trafalgar Square, the Strand and Covent Garden, Charing Cross is 49 m from the centre of Trafalgar Square, 83 m from the National Gallery, 628 m from the Royal Opera House and 634 m from Somerset House; its Underground platforms carry the Bakerloo and Northern lines and the rail station is served by Southeastern. From the National Portrait Gallery the same interchange measures 184 m to the Underground station and 247 m to the rail station, with Leicester Square 267 m. Covent Garden, on the Piccadilly line, is 208 m from the Royal Opera House, 288 m from the market building and 565 m from Somerset House; the station is itself Grade II, NHLE 1401025. Temple, on the Circle and District lines, is 190 m from Somerset House. Embankment is 300 m from Trafalgar Square, Leicester Square 378 m from the National Gallery and Piccadilly Circus 462 m from it, and the Piccadilly Circus booking hall concourse and the bronzework to its pavement subway entrances are Grade II, NHLE 1226877. Holborn, in Camden, is 771 m from Somerset House and is named by the Royal Opera House as a step-free alternative, along with Leicester Square and Tottenham Court Road.

For St James's, Mayfair and the Royal Parks, Green Park carries the Jubilee, Piccadilly and Victoria lines and is 299 m from the Royal Academy of Arts, 719 m from Apsley House, 775 m from Buckingham Palace and 873 m from St James's Park. Hyde Park Corner, on the Piccadilly line, is 100 m from Apsley House and 798 m from the palace. Victoria is 412 m from the palace and St James's Park station 584 m; St James's Park station is 277 m from the park of the same name. Piccadilly Circus is 445 m from the Royal Academy and Bond Street 841 m. Knightsbridge, on the Piccadilly line, is in Kensington and Chelsea, 675 m from Apsley House.

For Marylebone and Regent's Park, Bond Street is 339 m from the Wallace Collection by its Underground entrance and 407 m by its Elizabeth line entrance. Marble Arch is 625 m from the collection, Oxford Circus 727 m, Baker Street 745 m and Regent's Park station 804 m. Baker Street carries the Bakerloo, Circle, Hammersmith & City, Jubilee and Metropolitan lines and is the usual station for the south-west corner of The Regent's Park; Regent's Park station is on the Bakerloo line. Marylebone is the area's National Rail terminus, served by Chiltern Railways, with its Underground entrance 39 m and its rail entrance 59 m from the point measured. St John's Wood, on the Jubilee line, serves the north-west of the park and ZSL London Zoo.

Every distance above is a straight-line approximation, not a walking measurement.

faq.question: What are Westminster Abbey's opening hours, and what does it cost?
faq.answer: The abbey publishes its times day by day and they are not uniform. General Admittance runs 9.30am to 3.30pm Monday to Friday and 9am to 1pm on Saturday, and there is no General Admittance slot on Sunday, when St Margaret's Church opens 11am to 2pm, the Cellarium 9am to 3pm, the Kiosk 10am to 5pm and the Shop 9.30am to 4.30pm. In the operator's 17 June to 24 June and 2 September to 30 September 2026 band, admission is £31 for an adult, £28 for a visitor aged 65 and over, £28 for a student, £14 for a child aged 6 to 17 and free under 5, covering the cloisters, College Garden, Chapter House and Pyx Chamber. The abbey is at 20 Dean's Yard, SW1P 3PA, listed Grade I as NHLE 1291494.

faq.question: Which museums and galleries in Westminster are free?
faq.answer: The National Gallery gives general admission free and states that its paintings are on show 361 days a year free of charge, opening daily 10am to 6pm and until 9pm on Friday. Tate Britain is free with no need to book, opening Monday to Sunday 10.00 to 18.00. The Wallace Collection charges nothing for its permanent collection and opens daily 10.00 to 17.00. The Royal Academy of Arts keeps free displays including the John Madejski Fine Rooms and the Collection Gallery. Churchill War Rooms charges £34 for an adult, and Apsley House and Banqueting House are ticketed.

faq.question: When can I go inside Buckingham Palace?
faq.answer: The State Rooms open each summer, and the 2026 dates are 9 July to 27 September: opening 9:30 with last admission 17:30 and closing 19:30 until 31 August, then last admission 16:30 and closing 18:30 from 1 to 27 September, with the palace closed on Tuesdays and Wednesdays through September. From October to May it opens only on selected dates for small guided tours, starting between 10:00 and 15:30 and lasting around 1 hour 30 minutes. Standard admission is £33.00, or £37.00 with a donation, and the White Drawing Room will not be accessible during the 2026 Summer Opening because of the Buckingham Palace Reservicing programme.

faq.question: How many listed buildings does Westminster hold?
faq.answer: The National Heritage List for England records 4,003 listed-building entries inside the City of Westminster boundary as mapped by OpenStreetMap relation 51781: 206 at Grade I, 372 at Grade II* and 3,425 at Grade II. The unit is the list entry whose point falls inside the borough, not the individual building. The borough also holds 26 registered parks and gardens, five of them Grade I; three scheduled monuments, which carry no grade — the Chapter House and Pyx Chamber at Westminster Abbey, NHLE 1003579, the Jewel Tower, NHLE 1003580, and a subterranean commercial ice-well at Park Crescent West, NHLE 1427239; and one World Heritage Site, NHLE 1000095, inscribed in 1987.

faq.question: Which stations serve Westminster, and does the borough have an Overground or DLR station?
faq.answer: Twenty-nine distinct stations stand inside the City of Westminster. Four are National Rail termini: Charing Cross with Southeastern, Marylebone with Chiltern Railways, Paddington with Great Western Railway and Heathrow Express, and Victoria with Gatwick Express, Southeastern, Southern and Thameslink. Paddington, Bond Street and Tottenham Court Road take the Elizabeth line, the last straddling the Camden boundary. The borough has no Overground station, no DLR station and no tram stop. Queen's Park, which carries the Bakerloo line and the Overground Lioness line, is in Brent, and so are Kensal Green and Kilburn Park.

faq.question: Is the Royal Albert Hall in Westminster or in Kensington and Chelsea?
faq.answer: It is in the City of Westminster. The hall stands on Kensington Gore and is listed Grade I as NHLE 1217742, and the Albert Memorial on the same frontage is Grade I, NHLE 1217741. The three lamp standards outside the hall are Grade II entries in their own right and are not covered by the hall's entry, so the hall should never be described by their grade. Kensington Palace, 900 m west, is in Kensington and Chelsea: the borough boundary runs between the palace and the gardens.

photos.title: The west front of Westminster Abbey, Dean's Yard, Westminster
photos.description: The pale Portland stone west front seen head-on from the pavement, with the two square West Towers rising either side of the great traceried west window and the arched west door below it. Buttresses, pinnacles and rows of niche statues run up the facade, and the shot is framed tightly enough that the towers fill the top of the frame against open sky.

places.summary: Banqueting House is on Whitehall, SW1A 2ER, and is listed Grade I as NHLE 1357353. Historic Royal Palaces runs it on limited opening: a summer opening from 1 August to 20 September 2026, with separate Open Days and Members-Only Days. In the week of 31 August 2026 it opened 10:00 to 16:00 on Monday and Thursday to Sunday, closed on Tuesday and Wednesday, with last entry at 15:00. Tickets are £10.00 for an adult, free for a child aged 5 to 15 and free for members.

places.name: Churchill War Rooms
places.address: Clive Steps, King Charles Street, London SW1A 2AQ
places.summary: Churchill War Rooms is at Clive Steps, King Charles Street, SW1A 2AQ, in the basement of the Grade II* New Government Offices (HM Treasury), NHLE 1066103. It opens 9.30am to 6pm with last entry at 5pm, every day except 24 to 26 December, and admission is £34 for an adult, with members and under-fives free.
places.history: During the Second World War a group of basement offices in Whitehall, known as the Cabinet War Rooms, was occupied by leading government ministers, military strategists and Prime Minister Winston Churchill. Imperial War Museums calls it the secret underground headquarters of the Second World War, describes the rooms as left as they were in 1945 and gives the site as sitting under 12 feet of concrete and steel; the adjoining Churchill Museum covers Churchill's 90-year life. The designation is of the host building rather than of the museum: NHLE 1066103 is named New Government Offices (HM Treasury) and archway link with Foreign Office at east end of King Charles Street. The Grade II statue of Sir Winston Churchill stands about 250 m away in Parliament Square, NHLE 1392374.

places.name: Tate Britain
places.summary: Tate Britain is at Millbank, SW1P 4RG, and is listed Grade II* as NHLE 1222913 under the entry name TATE GALLERY. It opens Monday to Sunday 10.00 to 18.00, and Tate states that entry to the gallery is free with no need to book.
places.history: In 1892 a decision was made to build a new gallery for British art on the site of the former Millbank prison, with an anonymous donation from Henry Tate; the architect was Sidney Smith. The National Gallery of British Art, as Tate Britain was then called, was opened by the Prince of Wales on 21 July 1897 and opened to the public on 16 August 1897. Sir Henry Tate financed an extension that doubled the size of the original gallery with a further nine rooms including a sculpture hall, and he died on 5 December 1899. The Clore Gallery was opened on 1 April 1987, and two rooms are given to the work of Henry Moore. The gates, railings and gatepiers are a separate Grade II entry, NHLE 1267605; the statue of Sir John Millais at the west corner is Grade II, NHLE 1222797; and a K6 telephone kiosk outside is Grade II, NHLE 1436250. Pimlico station is 479 m away and Vauxhall, in Lambeth, 511 m.

places.name: Westminster Cathedral
places.summary: Westminster Cathedral is at 42 Francis Street, SW1P 1QW, and is listed Grade I as NHLE 1066500. It opens daily 7.30am to 7pm. The gift shop opens 10.30am to 4.30pm Wednesday to Sunday, and Clergy House Reception 9am to 5.20pm Monday to Friday and 10am to 1pm at weekends. Mass is celebrated on Sunday at 8am, 10am sung, 12 noon solemn and livestreamed, 5.30pm and 7pm.
places.history: The cathedral styles itself the Roman Catholic Metropolitan Cathedral of the Most Precious Blood, seat of the Archbishop of Westminster; it is neither Westminster Abbey nor St Paul's. It states that it receives no funding from the Vatican. Its own headings for what to see are An Architectural Gem, Art, Marbles & Mosaics, and Treasures. Victoria Underground station is 219 m away and London Victoria rail station 327 m; St James's Park station is 593 m.

places.name: The National Gallery
places.summary: The National Gallery is at Trafalgar Square, WC2N 5DN, with its visitor entrance in the Sainsbury Wing, and is listed Grade I as NHLE 1066236. It opens daily 10am to 6pm and until 9pm on Friday, closing 24 to 26 December and 1 January, and general admission is free.
places.history: The gallery holds the national collection of paintings in the Western European tradition from the 13th to the 19th centuries, over 2,600 works in all, and states that its paintings are on show 361 days a year, free of charge. It has undergone many transformations since its foundation in 1824, and a new Research Centre is opening in 2028. The Sainsbury Wing is a separate Grade I entry, NHLE 1451082. The statue of James II in front of the west wing is Grade I, NHLE 1217629, and the National Portrait Gallery next door is a separate Grade I entry, NHLE 1066285. Charing Cross station is 83 m away, Leicester Square 378 m and Piccadilly Circus 462 m.

places.name: National Portrait Gallery
places.summary: The National Portrait Gallery is on St Martin's Place, WC2H 0HE, and is listed Grade I as NHLE 1066285, a separate entry from the National Gallery next door, NHLE 1066236. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: The gallery stands immediately north-east of the National Gallery on St Martin's Place, between two other listed buildings on the same square: the Grade I Church of St Martin-in-the-Fields, NHLE 1217661, and the Grade II* St Martin's Vestry Hall, NHLE 1264790. Charing Cross Underground station, on the Bakerloo and Northern lines, is 184 m away and London Charing Cross rail station, served by Southeastern, 247 m; Leicester Square, on the Northern and Piccadilly lines, is 267 m. The 83 m figure often quoted for Charing Cross belongs to the National Gallery next door.

places.name: St Martin-in-the-Fields
places.summary: St Martin-in-the-Fields stands on Trafalgar Square, WC2N 4JJ, and is listed Grade I as NHLE 1217661 under the name CHURCH OF ST MARTIN IN THE FIELDS. The parish publishes its hours only two weeks ahead and they change week to week: in the week commencing 7 September the church opened 8.30am to 5pm on Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 8.30am to 7.30pm on Wednesday, 10.30am to 5pm on Saturday and 9am to 6pm on Sunday. The Cafe in the Crypt keeps its own separate hours.
places.history: The church is marking its 300th anniversary in 2026 and the parish refers to maintaining its 300-year-old church. It records a long tradition of hospitality, from pioneering work with homeless people through to hosting VIPs, politicians and dignitaries. The entry names on this site matter: the churchyard walls and railings are a separate Grade I entry, NHLE 1066237; a churchyard wall adjoining the crypt entrance is Grade II, NHLE 1264028; the John Law Baker memorial drinking fountain is Grade II, NHLE 1248613; and a drinking fountain attached to the church walls is Grade II, NHLE 1277825. The Grade II* St Martin's Vestry Hall, NHLE 1264790, St Martin's Vicarage, NHLE 1264791, and St Martin in the Fields Secondary School, NHLE 1236019, stand in the same block.

places.name: Trafalgar Square and Nelson's Column
places.summary: Trafalgar Square, WC2N 5DU, is a Grade I registered park and garden, NHLE 1001362, and the Nelson Monument, or Nelson's Column, is a separate Grade I listing, NHLE 1276052. Charing Cross Underground station is 49 m from the centre of the square.
places.history: Registered parks and gardens carry a grade, so the square is written as a Grade I registered park and garden rather than as a listed building. Two national collections and a Grade I parish church stand on the square: the National Gallery, NHLE 1066236, the National Portrait Gallery, NHLE 1066285, and St Martin-in-the-Fields, NHLE 1217661. The Grade I statue of James II stands in front of the National Gallery's west wing, NHLE 1217629. Embankment station is 300 m away, Leicester Square 498 m and Piccadilly Circus 580 m.

places.name: Somerset House
places.summary: Somerset House is on the Strand, WC2R 1LA, and is listed Grade I as NHLE 1237041 under the name SOMERSET HOUSE AND KING'S COLLEGE OLD BUILDING, an entry that covers the university building at the east end as well as the courtyard blocks. It is open to everyone seven days a week, 8am to 11pm.
places.history: The courtyard is the Edmond J. Safra Fountain Court. The City of London boundary runs east along the Strand from Somerset House, and the Grade I Church of St Mary le Strand, NHLE 1236753, stands in the roadway between. The Grade II* Savoy Chapel, the Queen's Chapel of the Savoy, is NHLE 1264731, and the Grade II Savoy Hotel is NHLE 1236709, both on the same stretch of the Strand. Temple station, on the Circle and District lines, is 190 m away; Covent Garden is 565 m and Charing Cross rail station 634 m.

places.name: Royal Opera House
places.summary: The Royal Opera House is on Bow Street, WC2E 9DD, and is listed Grade I as NHLE 1066392. It opens daily from 12 noon and closes after the evening performance; with no evening performance it closes at 11pm Monday to Saturday and 9pm on Sunday. Auditoriums open 30 minutes before each performance, and the box office opens Monday to Saturday from 12 noon until the start of the evening performance or 6pm.
places.history: The house is home to The Royal Ballet, The Royal Opera and The Orchestra of the Royal Opera House. The operator states that over one million people come through its doors each year and that it runs over 1,250 schools, community programmes and affordable performances. It names Covent Garden as its nearest Underground station, 208 m away, with step-free access at Leicester Square, Holborn and Tottenham Court Road; Covent Garden station is itself Grade II, NHLE 1401025. The Grade II* Covent Garden Market Building, NHLE 1066949, is about 100 m away, and the Grade I Church of St Paul, Covent Garden, is NHLE 1066487.

places.name: Buckingham Palace
places.summary: Buckingham Palace, SW1A 1AA, is listed Grade I as NHLE 1239087, and its grounds are separately a Grade II* registered park and garden, NHLE 1000795. The State Rooms open to visitors each summer and the 2026 dates are 9 July to 27 September: opening 9:30 with last admission 17:30 and closing 19:30 until 31 August, then last admission 16:30 and closing 18:30 from 1 to 27 September, with the palace closed on Tuesdays and Wednesdays through September. From October to May it opens only on selected dates for small guided tours, starting between 10:00 and 15:30 and lasting around 1 hour 30 minutes. Standard admission is £33.00, or £37.00 with a donation.
places.history: The Royal Collection Trust states that Queen Victoria was the first sovereign to live in the palace, in 1837, and that the White Drawing Room will not be accessible during the 2026 Summer Opening because of the Buckingham Palace Reservicing programme. At least a dozen further entries on the National Heritage List for England carry Buckingham Palace in their name, among them the Grade I Royal Mews, NHLE 1066364, the Grade I Riding School, NHLE 1239207, the Grade I Summer House in the garden, NHLE 1239210, the Grade I Waterloo Vase, NHLE 1239244, and four Grade II lamp posts at the gateway to the Royal Mews, NHLE 1239206. The Queen Victoria Memorial facing the palace is Grade I, NHLE 1273864, and its gates, gatepiers, balustrades and fountain are a further Grade I entry, NHLE 1239086. Victoria station is 412 m away, St James's Park 584 m, Green Park 775 m and Hyde Park Corner 798 m.

places.name: St James's Park
places.summary: St James's Park is on The Mall, SW1Y 5AA, and is a Grade I registered park and garden, NHLE 1000483. Its pedestrian gates open 5am to midnight. The Royal Parks manages it and describes its estate as covering over 5,000 acres of historic parkland.
places.history: It is one of five Grade I registered parks and gardens in the City of Westminster, with The Regent's Park, NHLE 1000246, Kensington Gardens, NHLE 1000340, Hyde Park, NHLE 1000814, and Trafalgar Square, NHLE 1001362; Green Park is Grade II*, NHLE 1000806. The park links Buckingham Palace at its west end to Horse Guards Parade at its east, with the Whitehall block between. St James's Park station, on the Circle and District lines, is 277 m away; Westminster is 569 m and Charing Cross 721 m.

places.name: Royal Academy of Arts
places.summary: The Royal Academy of Arts is at Burlington House, Piccadilly, W1J 0BD, and is listed Grade II* as NHLE 1226676 under the name Royal Academy including Burlington House and Galleries and Royal Academy Schools Buildings. It closes on Monday and opens Tuesday to Saturday 10am to 6pm and until 9pm on Friday; the operator publishes no Sunday row. Visitors are asked to use the Burlington House entrance until Spring 2027 while 6 Burlington Gardens is closed.
places.history: The RA was founded in 1768 by a group of 40 artists and architects who became the first Royal Academicians, and its first president was Sir Joshua Reynolds, whose statue stands outside Burlington House. Free displays include the John Madejski Fine Rooms and the Collection Gallery. A second Grade II* entry, NHLE 1291018, is named simply Royal Academy of Arts. The Grade II Burlington Arcade next door is NHLE 1066338 and the Grade II* Ritz Hotel is NHLE 1226499. Green Park station, on the Jubilee, Piccadilly and Victoria lines, is 299 m away; Piccadilly Circus is 445 m and Bond Street 841 m.

places.name: Apsley House
places.address: 149 Piccadilly, Hyde Park Corner, London W1J 7NT
places.summary: Apsley House is at 149 Piccadilly, Hyde Park Corner, W1J 7NT, and is listed Grade I as NHLE 1226873. English Heritage opens it Wednesday to Sunday, 11am to 5pm, with last entry at 4.30pm. Hyde Park Corner Underground station, on the Piccadilly line, is 100 m away.
places.history: The house was designed and built between 1771 and 1778 for Lord Chancellor Henry, 1st Baron Apsley, later 2nd Earl Bathurst, by Robert Adam, at a cost of £10,000. Wellington became Prime Minister in January 1828 and commissioned further changes that year, including the new staircase and the Waterloo Gallery on the west front; Benjamin Dean Wyatt's final bill exceeded £64,000, and Wellington bought the freehold in January 1830 for £9,532. The collection includes work by Velazquez, Rubens, Goya, Titian and Bruegel. The Wellington Museum Act was signed in 1947 and Apsley House opened to the public in 1952, the centenary of the death of the 1st Duke of Wellington. Knightsbridge station, in Kensington and Chelsea, is 675 m away and Green Park 719 m.

places.name: Royal Albert Hall
places.summary: The Royal Albert Hall stands on Kensington Gore, in the City of Westminster, and is listed Grade I as NHLE 1217742. Wikidata carries the same list entry number for it and gives its borough as the City of Westminster. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: The three lamp standards outside the hall are Grade II entries in their own right and are not part of the hall's own entry, NHLE 1217742, so the hall itself should never be described by their grade. The Albert Memorial, Grade I, NHLE 1217741, stands on the same frontage and is also in the City of Westminster. Kensington Palace, 900 m west, is in Kensington and Chelsea, and the borough boundary runs between the palace and the gardens.

places.name: The Wallace Collection
places.address: Hertford House, Manchester Square, London W1U 3BN
places.summary: The Wallace Collection is at Hertford House, Manchester Square, W1U 3BN, and opens daily 10.00 to 17.00, closing on 24, 25 and 26 December. Entry to the permanent collection is free. It is a national museum of painting, sculpture, furniture, arms and armour, and porcelain.
places.history: The collection was built over the 18th and 19th centuries by the Marquesses of Hertford and Sir Richard Wallace, and was given to the British nation in 1897 by Lady Wallace so that it could be kept together. Hertford House is listed Grade II, NHLE 1239252; its forecourt walls, gate piers and railings are a separate Grade II entry, NHLE 1239308, and the drinking fountain in the forecourt is Grade II*, NHLE 1277828. Manchester Square itself, with Portman Square, is a Grade II registered park and garden, NHLE 1000820. Bond Street station is 339 m away by its Underground entrance and 407 m by its Elizabeth line entrance; Marble Arch is 625 m, Oxford Circus 727 m and Baker Street 745 m.

places.name: The Regent's Park
places.summary: The Regent's Park is entered from the Inner Circle, NW1 4NR, and is a Grade I registered park and garden, NHLE 1000246. Its pedestrian gates open 5am to 8pm and its vehicle gates 7am to midnight.
places.history: The Royal Parks records over 120 species of bird in the park each year, 5,000 varieties of tree, areas of wild meadow, historic grasslands and a breeding population of hedgehogs. The park lies in the City of Westminster; Primrose Hill, which The Royal Parks manages together with it as one operational unit, lies north of the Regent's Canal in Camden. The Nash terraces around the Outer Circle are listed at Grade I in their own right: 1-43 Clarence Terrace is NHLE 1357311. Regent's Park station, on the Bakerloo line, serves the park, and Baker Street, carrying the Bakerloo, Circle, Hammersmith & City, Jubilee and Metropolitan lines, serves its south-west corner.

places.name: ZSL London Zoo
places.address: Outer Circle, The Regent's Park, London
places.summary: ZSL London Zoo stands inside The Regent's Park, off the Outer Circle. Its main entrance, the boating lake and the Inner Circle side are in the City of Westminster, and the northern fringe along the Outer Circle is in Camden. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: Four structures at the zoo are on the National Heritage List for England: the Elephant and Rhinoceros Pavilion, Grade II*, NHLE 1323694; the Snowdon Aviary, Grade II*, NHLE 1323695; the west footbridge, Grade II, NHLE 1119765; and the London Zoo War Memorial, Grade II, NHLE 1434655. The zoo sits within The Regent's Park, itself a Grade I registered park and garden, NHLE 1000246. St John's Wood station, on the Jubilee line, serves the north-west of the park and the zoo.

links.note: Battersea Power Station and Nine Elms face Pimlico and Tate Britain across the Thames; the boroughs share the river between Vauxhall and Chelsea bridges.
Queen's Park is a ward name in Westminster and a park in Brent, and Paddington Old Cemetery carries a Westminster parish name on Willesden Lane in Brent.
The Regent's Canal boundary stones by Hampstead Road Lock, NHLE 1248422 and 1248423, are Westminster's while the lock is Camden's; Primrose Hill is Camden's.
The Royal Albert Hall and the Albert Memorial stand on Kensington Gore in Westminster; Kensington Palace, 900 m west, is in Kensington and Chelsea.

entries.name: Westminster Abbey
entries.note: The coronation church since 1066, listed Grade I as NHLE 1291494; General Admittance 9.30am to 3.30pm Monday to Friday and 9am to 1pm Saturday, £31 for an adult.

entries.name: Houses of Parliament
entries.note: Barry and Pugin's palace of 1840, Grade I as NHLE 1226284 and part of the World Heritage Site NHLE 1000095; guided tours are free for UK residents.

entries.name: Banqueting House, Whitehall
entries.note: Inigo Jones's hall with the Rubens ceiling opens only in limited seasons — 1 August to 20 September 2026, plus Open Days — so check the operator before setting out.

entries.name: Churchill War Rooms
entries.note: The Cabinet War Rooms under 12 feet of concrete and steel, left as they were in 1945; 9.30am to 6pm daily except 24 to 26 December, £34 for an adult.

entries.name: Tate Britain
entries.note: British art on the site of the Millbank prison, opened to the public on 16 August 1897; 10.00 to 18.00 daily and free, with two rooms of Henry Moore.

entries.name: Westminster Cathedral
entries.note: The Roman Catholic Metropolitan Cathedral of the Most Precious Blood, Grade I as NHLE 1066500, open daily 7.30am to 7pm, 219 m from Victoria Underground.

entries.name: The National Gallery
entries.note: Over 2,600 works, with the paintings on show 361 days a year, free of charge; 10am to 6pm daily and to 9pm Friday, entrance through the Sainsbury Wing.

entries.name: National Portrait Gallery
entries.note: Grade I as NHLE 1066285, on St Martin's Place beside the National Gallery; 184 m from Charing Cross Underground. No source states its opening hours.

entries.name: St Martin-in-the-Fields
entries.note: A parish church marking its 300th anniversary in 2026, Grade I as NHLE 1217661; hours are published two weeks ahead and change week to week.

entries.name: Trafalgar Square and Nelson's Column
entries.note: A Grade I registered park and garden, NHLE 1001362, with the Nelson Monument as a separate Grade I entry, NHLE 1276052; Charing Cross is 49 m away.

entries.name: Somerset House
entries.note: Grade I as NHLE 1237041, open to everyone 8am to 11pm seven days a week around the Edmond J. Safra Fountain Court; Temple station is 190 m away.

entries.name: Royal Opera House
entries.note: Home of The Royal Ballet and The Royal Opera on Bow Street, Grade I as NHLE 1066392; open from 12 noon daily, with Covent Garden station 208 m away.

entries.name: Buckingham Palace State Rooms
entries.note: Open 9 July to 27 September 2026, closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays in September; £33.00, or £37.00 with a donation. October to May it is selected dates only.

entries.name: St James's Park
entries.note: A Grade I registered park and garden, NHLE 1000483, running from Buckingham Palace to Horse Guards Parade; pedestrian gates open 5am to midnight.

entries.name: Royal Academy of Arts
entries.note: Founded 1768 at Burlington House, Grade II* as NHLE 1226676; closed Monday, 10am to 6pm Tuesday to Saturday and to 9pm Friday, with free displays.

entries.name: Apsley House
entries.note: Wellington's house at Hyde Park Corner, Grade I as NHLE 1226873, opened to the public in 1952; Wednesday to Sunday 11am to 5pm, last entry 4.30pm.

entries.name: Royal Albert Hall
entries.note: On Kensington Gore in the City of Westminster, Grade I as NHLE 1217742, with the Albert Memorial, NHLE 1217741, on the same frontage.

entries.name: The Wallace Collection
entries.note: Given to the nation in 1897 and kept in Hertford House; paintings, furniture, arms and armour and porcelain, free, daily 10.00 to 17.00.

entries.name: The Regent's Park
entries.note: A Grade I registered park and garden, NHLE 1000246, with 5,000 varieties of tree and over 120 species of bird a year; gates open 5am to 8pm.

entries.name: ZSL London Zoo
entries.note: Inside The Regent's Park off the Outer Circle, holding the Grade II* Snowdon Aviary, NHLE 1323695, and Elephant and Rhinoceros Pavilion, NHLE 1323694.
